core_obligations: Write both sides as derived limits (proof lines 5899-5902): the truncation theorem gives the complex as the derived limit of its truncations and commutation with derived limits gives the pushforward as the derived limit of the pushed forward truncations.

Show the groups are eventually constant (proof lines 5903-5912): evaluating at the members of a cofinal system of coverings, the assumption of the second situation makes the cohomology group of the truncation independent of the truncation index once that index is large compared with the degree and the dimension bound; the author records that the details of this step are omitted.

Identify the limit and conclude (proof lines 5913-5963): applying the constancy in two consecutive degrees and the commutation of cohomology with the derived limit gives the displayed identification of the cohomology of the pushforward with the limit of the cohomology of the truncations, and the long exact sequence of the truncation triangle then shows that the map from the pushforward to the pushforward of a sufficiently negative truncation is an isomorphism in the asserted degrees.
proof_roadmap: Rewrite the complex and its pushforward as derived limits of truncations.
Evaluate on a cofinal system of coverings and use the dimension bound to make the cohomology groups independent of the truncation index.
Conclude by the description of the cohomology of a derived limit and the truncation triangle.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a second version, with slightly changed hypotheses, of the Olsson-Laszlo boundedness statement for a morphism of ringed sites: under the two Olsson-Laszlo situations and the vanishing of the higher direct images above a fixed degree, the cohomology sheaves of the derived pushforward agree with those of the pushforward of a sufficiently negative truncation in degrees at least N - n (statement lines 5875-5895). The proof is a complete derived limit argument: the complex and its pushforward are written as derived limits of truncations (proof lines 5899-5902); evaluating at a cofinal system of coverings and using the dimension bound in the second situation shows that the relevant cohomology groups are eventually constant, independently of the truncation index (proof lines 5903-5912); and the description of the cohomology of a derived limit, applied in two consecutive degrees, together with the long exact sequence of the truncation triangle, yields the asserted isomorphism (proof lines 5913-5963). The non-formal content is the derived limit bookkeeping and the use of the dimension bound to obtain constancy. The claim is H2: a structured reduction with each input and each degree estimate named.
